title: Find the astronomical point
brief:
The ward tracks **medication administration errors per 1,000 doses**, monthly (median = 5). One month stands out. The rota that month leaned heavily on locum staff.

Using Provost & Murray's **astronomical-point rule** — one point that is obviously, strikingly different from all the others — click the single point that is the signal.

(Keyboard users: press Tab to enter the chart, Left/Right arrow to move between points, Enter to select.)

exhibit.title: Medication administration errors per 1,000 doses — monthly

task.stem: Click the single point that is the astronomical-point signal. Submit when it is selected.

debrief.correct: That's the one. Month 10 reads 19 per 1,000 doses against a median of 5 — nearly **four times** the usual level and far outside the ordinary month-to-month band (4–6). One point that obviously different is an **astronomical point**, and it fires on its own — you do not need a run around it. Crucially, it points you to **investigate that specific month** (the locum-heavy rota), not to conclude the whole system has deteriorated. Fix the assignable cause; don't tamper with a system that is otherwise stable.
debrief.wrong: The astronomical-point rule is the eyeball test: **one point strikingly different from all the rest.** Every month sits in a tight 4–6 band except month 10, which jumps to 19 — about four times the median of 5. That single point is the signal. It tells you to investigate *what was different that month* (here, a locum-heavy rota), not to overhaul a system that is otherwise in control.
debrief.rule_cited: Provost & Murray (2nd ed.) — Astronomical-point rule (one point obviously different from the others); investigate the special cause, do not tamper with the stable system.
